modules.name: Lateral system selector by height, slenderness and seismic category
modules.design_question: Which lateral systems (core walls, core-outrigger, mega-frame, diagrid, buttressed core) suit this height, slenderness and Vancouver SC4, and which code route and podium rule must the scheme satisfy?
modules.effort: ~5 person-days after 13 Nov (whole SC4 rule column double-entered, wall-continuity rule, elevation view). Drift screening waits for the M04 wind engine (roadmap).
inputs: Layer 0: tower massing (height, storeys, floor plates, setbacks, transfer levels)
Layer 0 program tags (office, residential, hotel, core, mechanical) to propose outrigger floors
P10-M02: H/w_eff and wind class
P10-M03: Seismic Category, site designation, route flags
P10-M05: core share, irregularity flags incl. Types 4 and 5, wall continuity
ADVANCED presets: primary structural material (concrete, steel, composite, timber-hybrid)
outputs: candidate_systems[]: {system, feasibility, code_route_state (listed SFRS + outrigger elements | equivalence route | unlisted), reasons[]}
sfrs_choice: {type, Rd, Ro, height_cap_m} or 'unlisted'
wall_continuity_status: red/green per storey (hard rule, from P10-M05)
outrigger_levels[] (default = mechanical floors) and differential-shortening warning
structure_diagram_spec: JSON consumed by PRES structural-strategy drawings

parameters.name: Tower height H
parameters.relationship: H up -> wind drift, acceleration and overturning grow faster than linearly, pushing the choice from core-only walls toward perimeter-engaged systems; steel frames alone become uneconomic above about 40 storeys (secondary sources).

parameters.name: Seismic Category (Vancouver = SC4)
parameters.relationship: Vancouver is SC4 (IE*S(0.2) about 1.04 g > 0.75). SC4 caps: moderately ductile concrete walls 60 m; ductile BRBF, moderately ductile concrete MRF and plate walls 40 m. Supertowers need ductile or coupled walls, or proven equivalence.

parameters.name: SFRS wall continuity
parameters.unit: count of storeys with a wall break
parameters.relationship: Ta >= 1 s and IE*S(1.0) > 0.25 (every VTC tower): SFRS shear walls must run continuously to the foundation, no Type 4 or 5. Any core transfer or offset is red; open podium spaces must wrap around the core.

parameters.name: Slenderness H/w_eff and sqrt(wd)/H
parameters.relationship: H/w up -> across-wind acceleration and overturning rise; when sqrt(wd)/H is below 1/3, across-wind accelerations usually exceed along-wind, favouring perimeter engagement and added damping.

parameters.name: Transfers and outrigger floors
parameters.relationship: Gravity-column transfers are possible; any SFRS wall transfer is red. Stiff transfer or outrigger floors shorten the real period below empirical Ta, so Ta-based forces may be unconservative: flag for dynamic analysis.

parameters.name: Primary structural material
parameters.relationship: Prescriptive timber frames stop at 18 storeys / 76 m (BCBC 3.2.2.93) and timber SFRS at 20 m at SC4, so supertall lateral systems must be concrete, steel or composite; timber stays in a firewall-separated podium building.

parameters.name: Outrigger / belt-truss use
parameters.relationship: No outrigger SFRS is listed in NBC 2020. Usual route: listed core walls as SFRS, outriggers as capacity-protected elements (lowest RdRo for combined systems, special study likely); otherwise equivalence route or unlisted.

metrics.name: Code route of selected system
metrics.good: Listed SFRS with no SC4 height cap (ductile coupled, partially coupled or shear walls Rd 3.5-4.0; ductile concrete MRF; steel ductile MRF, EBF, plate walls). Whole SC4 column loaded from JSON.
metrics.bad: Unlisted SFRS (Rd = Ro = 1.0; 'other' SFRS not permitted at SC3-SC4) or a capped type above its cap (e.g. moderately ductile concrete walls above 60 m, ductile BRBF above 40 m).
metrics.basis: NBC 2020 Table 4.1.8.9 SC4 column (2nd printing, 2025); Commentary J paras 213-214 on equivalence; 4.1.8.9(3) lowest RdRo and (5) equivalence for combined systems.
metrics.method: Table lookup by SFRS type, height and Seismic Category; three route states for outrigger schemes

metrics.name: SFRS wall continuity (NBC 4.1.8.10(4))
metrics.good: Every SFRS shear wall continuous from top to foundation; no Type 4 or 5 irregularity.
metrics.bad: Any wall that ends, steps or is transferred, including at the podium: red, not permitted. No 'needs NLDA' route.
metrics.basis: NBC 2020 4.1.8.10(4), applies where Ta >= 1.0 s and IE*S(1.0) > 0.25; downtown X450 S(1.0) = 0.43 g (r1 reviewer-read, 2nd printing).
metrics.method: Read M05 continuity flags per storey and colour the elevation

metrics.name: Storeys versus system envelope (editable)
metrics.good: <= 70 storeys for core / shear-wall-frame without outriggers
metrics.bad: > 70 storeys core-only, or > ~40 storeys steel frame only
metrics.basis: Secondary precedent statements only (shear-wall frame to 70 storeys; steel frames inefficient above 40). CVU guides paywalled; editable team assumption.
metrics.method: Compare storeys (H / floor-to-floor) with envelope table

metrics.name: Service-wind drift per storey
metrics.good: <= hs/500 at every storey under service wind (Iw SLS = 0.75) with Dynamic Procedure pressures p = Iw q Ce Ct Cg Cp.
metrics.bad: > hs/500 at any storey. Top drift H/500 is only a secondary Commentary I guide (range 1/250-1/1000).
metrics.basis: NBC 2020 4.1.3.5(3) (r1 reviewer quote), Table 4.1.7.3, 4.1.7.8; Commentary I paras 106-107 are guidance only.
metrics.method: Equivalent-cantilever or stick model with editable effective-EI multiplier, loaded by the M04 wind engine (roadmap)

modules.method: 1) Read H, storeys, H/w (M02), Seismic Category and route flags (M03), core, continuity and irregularity flags (M05), material preset. 2) Filter the catalogue (core walls, core + outriggers or belt trusses, mega-frame, diagrid, buttressed core, coupled walls, steel EBF/BRB hybrids, timber-hybrid) by the whole SC4 column of Table 4.1.8.9, with three route states for outriggers. 3) Hard rule: SFRS walls continuous to the foundation, so any Type 4 or 5 flag is red. 4) Apply EMTC limits (M06) and editable storey envelopes. 5) When the M04 wind engine exists, screen per-storey service-wind drift against hs/500; show H/500 as secondary. 6) Score survivors on drift margin, core share, transfers and material intensity (M08) with user weights. 7) Output a shortlist with reasons, never a single best; unlisted systems go to alternative solution plus the review tiers of M03.
visualization: Matrix heat-map: rows = candidate systems, columns = code route, wall continuity, height envelope, drift, core share; green/amber/red cells; a click opens the clause or the editable assumption.
Tower elevation (SVG): core, outrigger levels, red storeys where SFRS walls are discontinuous, marker lines at 60 m, 76 m (EMTC cap) and 70 storeys.
Per-threshold badges: 'verified' (clause link), 'team assumption' (editable), 'FALSE ASSUMPTION' (special colour).
modules.human_judgment: Choosing and defending the system is an engineering and design judgement (intent, constructability, owner risk, alternative-solution strategy with the engineer of record); the tool filters, flags code routes and shows trade-offs.
modules.limits: Screening only; no member sizing. Envelopes and effective-EI multipliers are editable presets. Outrigger effectiveness, differential shortening, creep and construction sequence are not modelled (warning only for concrete core with steel or composite perimeter). Not a substitute for an engineer or peer review.

modules.name: Slenderness, effective width and wind-sensitivity class
modules.design_question: How slender is each tower, and which NBC 2020 wind procedure does that force: Dynamic, or the mandatory Wind Tunnel Procedure (very dynamically sensitive, wake buffeting, f1 at or below 0.25 Hz)?
modules.effort: ~1.5 person-days for 13 Nov (rules only: mesh slicing, azimuth sweep, clause table); polar plot and wake rays can follow.
inputs: Layer 0 tower meshes (one per tower) with storey table
Site plan rotation relative to true north
Context building massing (existing and approved towers) where available
Optional f1 from a dynamic model (P10-M08, roadmap); never the code Ta from P10-M03
outputs: tower_wind_class[]: {tower_id, H, w_eff_min, d_eff, H_over_w, sqrt_wd_over_H, class, governing_trigger, vortex_flag, tunnel_required}
w_eff_by_azimuth[36]
slenderness_band enum (consumed by P10-M01, P10-M04)
context_flags[]: possible wake-buffeting sources

parameters.name: Tower height H
parameters.relationship: H > 60 m makes any building dynamically sensitive (4.1.7.2(2)(b)), so every 244-305 m tower uses the Dynamic or Wind Tunnel Procedure. H >= about 180 m defaults tunnel_required = true unless a model f1 > 0.25 Hz is supplied.

parameters.name: Effective width w and depth d
parameters.relationship: w = sum(h_i w_i)/sum(h_i); d likewise. w down -> H/w up: above 4 dynamically sensitive, above 6 with human occupancy very dynamically sensitive (tunnel mandatory); sqrt(wd)/H < 1/3 means across-wind governs.

parameters.name: Lowest natural frequency f1 (dynamic model only)
parameters.relationship: f1 between 0.25 and 1 Hz -> dynamically sensitive; f1 <= 0.25 Hz -> very dynamically sensitive, tunnel mandatory. Code Ta is for seismic loads, not wind (Commentary J); approximate frequency formulas are cautioned (Commentary I para 114).

parameters.name: Plan shape (Strouhal number S)
parameters.relationship: Circular plans S about 1/5; non-circular (rectangular, polygonal) about 1/7. V_Hc = f_n D / S, so S = 1/7 gives a 40% higher V_Hc than 1/5. Para 105 recommends tunnel tests for non-circular sections.

parameters.name: Neighbouring towers (context)
parameters.relationship: Upwind towers of similar height can cause wake buffeting or channelling; NBC 4.1.7.1(4) then requires the Wind Tunnel Procedure but gives no distance trigger, so the tool flags, not decides.

parameters.name: Tapering, setbacks, twist
parameters.relationship: These change effective width with height and can disrupt coherent vortex shedding: Burj Khalifa's 27 setbacks, Shanghai Tower's 120-degree twist (claimed 24% load cut). Precedent claims need tunnel confirmation.

metrics.name: Wind procedure class (governing trigger)
metrics.good: Static procedure only if H <= 60 m, f1 >= 1 Hz and H/w <= 4: not reachable for 244-305 m towers.
metrics.bad: Very dynamically sensitive (f1 <= 0.25 Hz, or H/w > 6 with human occupancy) or wake buffeting possible: Wind Tunnel Procedure mandatory.
metrics.basis: NBC 2020 Div B 4.1.7.1(2)-(4) and 4.1.7.2(2)-(3), 2nd printing amended pages 4-29 and 4-44.
metrics.method: Rule evaluation; colour by the governing trigger, not by H/w alone

metrics.name: Aspect ratio H / w_eff,min (all wind directions)
metrics.good: <= 4 (not dynamically sensitive by slenderness; H > 60 m still overrides)
metrics.bad: > 6 with human occupancy -> tunnel mandatory; 4-6 = dynamically sensitive
metrics.basis: NBC 2020 4.1.7.2(2)(c), (3)(b); w from wi and hi as defined in 4.1.7.8(4); check the equation graphic when coding.
metrics.method: Height-weighted effective width per storey slice, minimum over azimuths

metrics.name: Default tunnel requirement for supertall towers (editable)
metrics.good: Model f1 > 0.25 Hz supplied: Dynamic Procedure possible
metrics.bad: H >= 180 m with no model f1: tunnel_required = true
metrics.basis: 180 m is a team threshold from tall-tower f1 typically near or below 0.25 Hz; Commentary I para 114 cautions against approximate frequency formulas.
metrics.method: If no model f1, set tunnel_required for H >= threshold

metrics.name: Vortex-shedding slenderness H/D
metrics.bad: > 5 -> vortex-shedding check: V_Hc = f_n D / S, S = 1/7 non-circular, 1/5 circular; tunnel required for non-circular
metrics.basis: NBC Commentary I paras 103-105 (S about 1/5 only for large circular structures, 1/7 non-circular).
metrics.method: H divided by least plan dimension D

metrics.name: Across-wind dominance parameter sqrt(wd)/H
metrics.good: >= 1/3 (along-wind may govern accelerations)
metrics.bad: < 1/3 (across-wind accelerations exceed along-wind)
metrics.basis: Commentary I para 108 criterion with w, d, H; d uses the same weighting with d_i (r1 reviewer-read); check equation graphic.
metrics.method: Computed from w, d, H

metrics.name: Lowest natural frequency triggers (model f1 only)
metrics.good: >= 1 Hz (not expected for supertall)
metrics.bad: <= 0.25 Hz -> tunnel mandatory; 0.25-1 Hz -> Dynamic or Wind Tunnel Procedure. Code Ta (3.1-3.7 s walls, 0.27-0.32 Hz) must not be used.
metrics.basis: NBC 2020 4.1.7.2(2)(a), (3)(a); Commentary J: empirical Ta only for seismic loads, not wind.
metrics.method: f1 from stick-model modal analysis (P10-M08, roadmap) or user input

metrics.name: Super-slender band (editable)
metrics.bad: > 10 (expect TMD, aerodynamic shaping or windbreak floors)
metrics.basis: No sourced threshold. Precedent: 432 Park Avenue (about 15:1) uses two ~540 t TMDs and 12-storey windbreaks, with reported occupant complaints (secondary).
metrics.method: Compare H/w_eff with editable band

metrics.name: Wake-buffeting / channelling potential
metrics.good: No taller or similar-height building upwind within the modelled context
metrics.bad: Similar-height towers upwind (flag only; default trigger >= 0.5 H, editable) -> Wind Tunnel Procedure
metrics.basis: NBC 4.1.7.1(4) mandates the tunnel where buffeting or channelling is possible but gives no numeric trigger.
metrics.method: Upwind ray-casting from each tower

modules.method: For each tower mesh, slice at every storey. For each wind azimuth (10-degree steps in true north, after the site-plan rotation) project the slice onto the normal to the wind to get w_i and d_i. Compute w = sum(h_i w_i)/sum(h_i) and d likewise, and take the minimum w over azimuths. Compute H/w, sqrt(wd)/H against 1/3, H/D, and V_Hc = f_n D/S with S = 1/7 (non-circular) or 1/5 (circular). Apply NBC triggers: H > 60 m, H/w of 4 and 6, f1 of 1 Hz and 0.25 Hz; colour by the governing trigger. With no model f1 and H >= 180 m (editable), set tunnel_required = true; reject code Ta as f1. Ray-cast upwind to flag towers >= 0.5 H as wake sources. Print that CFD cannot give specified loads (4.1.7.1(6)).
visualization: Tower elevation coloured by governing trigger (green only if every trigger clears; amber 4-6; red tunnel mandatory) with the 60 m line and labelled H/w_eff.
Polar (radar) plot of w_eff versus wind azimuth with the minimum highlighted and the rotated site north drawn.
Site-plan overlay: upwind rays and flagged wake sources; badges link to NBC clause numbers.
modules.human_judgment: Whether neighbouring towers cause buffeting or channelling, whether top storeys count as human occupancy, and whether to reshape the tower; the final wind procedure is set by the wind engineer and tunnel test.
modules.limits: Classification only; predicts no loads or accelerations. Effective-width and across-wind equations must be checked against PDF graphics. Wake distance and the 180 m default are team assumptions. Approved-but-unbuilt towers are modelled by hand. Does not replace the wind engineer.

modules.name: Vancouver seismic screening (NBC 2020 / BCBC 2024 / VBBL 2025)
modules.design_question: What seismic hazard, Seismic Category and code route does this tower face in downtown Vancouver, and which flags (dynamic analysis, wall continuity, nonlinear analysis, review tiers) apply?
modules.effort: 13 Nov core ~3 person-days (hazard fetch, SC, Ta, route flags). v1 adds ~3 (Mv/J base shear, drift multiplier, Vd floor); NLDA support is roadmap.
inputs: Latitude/longitude of the VTC block (default downtown 49.2827, -123.1207)
Site designation: measured Vs30 (X_V), class A-E (X_S) or X_F; default X450
SFRS choice from P10-M01 (default ductile concrete wall)
Layer 0 height, storeys, and irregularity and continuity flags from P10-M05
Importance category (normal, high importance, post-disaster)
Seismic weight W preset (GFA x kN/m2) until P10-M08 exists
outputs: design_spectrum: Sa(T) at 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10 s plus PGA, for 2% and 10% in 50 years
seismic_category (SC1-SC4)
Ta_empirical (seismic only), T1_model and period caps
route_flags: {static_not_permitted, dynamic_required, wall_continuity, type9_nlda, special_study_panel, unlisted_sfrs, egbc_review, non_sfrs_elastic_check}
v1 screening: V/W, Ft, base moment with J, drift = elastic x RdRo/IE, Vd floor

parameters.name: Site designation / Vs30 and hazard source
parameters.relationship: Vs30 down -> Sa up, most at long periods: downtown 2%/50 yr Sa(1.0) is 0.43 g (X450), 0.64 g (X250), 0.82 g (X_S class D). X_S is more conservative than measured X_V. Long periods are interface-driven.

parameters.name: Fundamental period Ta (seismic only)
parameters.relationship: Taller or more flexible -> longer Ta (0.05 hn^3/4 walls: 3.1-3.7 s at 244-305 m). Ta >= 1 s triggers wall continuity. Stiff outrigger floors can make the true period shorter than Ta, so Ta forces may be unconservative.

parameters.name: Ductility and overstrength Rd x Ro
parameters.relationship: Rd x Ro up -> design base shear V = S(Ta) Mv IE W/(RdRo) falls, but design drift = elastic drift x RdRo/IE rises (ductile walls RdRo 5.6). Only SFRS types permitted at the SC and height count.

parameters.name: Higher-mode factor Mv and moment reduction J (v1)
parameters.relationship: Spectral ratio S(0.2)/S(5.0) up (Vancouver about 1.04/0.0735 = 14) -> Mv up for walls and J down, so tall wall towers attract more base shear and less moment reduction than the fundamental mode implies.

parameters.name: Importance category
parameters.relationship: Importance up -> stricter drift limit: 0.025 hs normal, 0.020 hs High Importance, 0.010 hs post-disaster; larger IE also raises the Seismic Category input IE*S(0.2).

parameters.name: Irregularity types 1-10
parameters.relationship: Types 4/5 (SFRS wall discontinuity) banned when Ta >= 1 s and IE*S(1.0) > 0.25; Type 6 only at SC1. Type 9 (alpha > 0.1 self-centering, 0.03 other) multiplies drift by 1.2; NLDA only above 2x alpha and IE*S(0.2) >= 0.5.

parameters.name: Analysis and SFRS route (listed / NLDA / unlisted)
parameters.relationship: Listed SFRS with response spectrum needs baseline EGBC independent review; NLDA adds a special-study panel (3 experts or more); unlisted SFRS or equivalence adds the City alternative-solution panel.

parameters.name: Gravity framing outside the SFRS
parameters.relationship: SC4 Normal Importance towers over 30 m: framing not counted as SFRS must stay elastic at 10%-in-50-year forces with RdRo = 1.3, so gravity columns and slab-column connections get larger or more ductile.

metrics.name: Seismic Category
metrics.good: SC1-SC2 (static method permitted; not applicable here)
metrics.basis: NBC 2020 Table 4.1.8.5-B; NRCan hazard API values for downtown Vancouver, Vs30 450 m/s.
metrics.method: Threshold lookup on IE*S(0.2) and IE*S(1.0)

metrics.name: Design hazard values used
metrics.good: NRCan 2020 values at the block lat/lon and site designation; downtown X450, 2%/50 yr (g): 0.2 s 1.04, 0.5 s 0.748, 1.0 s 0.429, 2.0 s 0.266, 5.0 s 0.0735, 10 s 0.0323, PGA 0.446.
metrics.bad: NBC 2015 / VBBL 2019 values (Sa(0.2) about 0.85 g); Table C-3's 0.848 g is a Part 9 value carried over from 2015.
metrics.basis: NRCan API queried 21 Oct 2026; Commentary J Table J-2 is a rounded fallback (1.1, 0.77, 0.44, 0.27, 0.075, 0.033, PGA 0.46); new VBBL seismic rules from 15 Sep 2026.
metrics.method: API fetch (CORS open) or pasted values, then NBC interpolation

metrics.name: Analysis route and dynamic base-shear floor
metrics.good: Dynamic analysis (response spectrum or NLDA); Vd >= 0.8 V regular, 1.0 V irregular (4.1.8.12(8)-(9))
metrics.bad: Equivalent static as final design: only SC1-SC2, regular < 60 m with Ta < 2 s, or irregular (Types 2-6, 8) < 20 m with Ta < 0.5 s
metrics.basis: NBC 2020 Div B 4.1.8.7(1) and 4.1.8.12(8)-(9) (r1 reviewer-read); Commentary J.
metrics.method: Rule evaluation

metrics.name: SFRS wall continuity and Type 4/5/6
metrics.good: Ta < 1 s or IE*S(1.0) <= 0.25 (not the case for VTC towers)
metrics.bad: Ta >= 1 s and IE*S(1.0) > 0.25: SFRS walls continuous to foundation; any Type 4, 5 or 6 flag is not permitted
metrics.basis: NBC 2020 4.1.8.10(1), (4) (r1 reviewer-read, 2nd printing); (1) and (2) seen on amended page 4-63.
metrics.method: Rule evaluation using P10-M05 flags

metrics.name: Type 9 gravity-induced lateral demand route
metrics.good: alpha <= 0.1 (self-centering) or 0.03 (other SFRS): no Type 9
metrics.bad: Type 9: drift x 1.2; NLDA with vertical motion only if alpha > 2x the limit and IE*S(0.2) >= 0.5
metrics.basis: NBC 2020 Table 4.1.8.6 Type 9; 4.1.8.10(7)-(9) (r1 reviewer-read).
metrics.method: Encode alpha limits, 1.2 drift factor and NLDA trigger separately

metrics.name: Interstorey drift at design-level shaking
metrics.good: Elastic drift incl. accidental torsion x RdRo/IE (x 1.2 if Type 9) <= 0.025 hs normal, 0.020 hs High, 0.010 hs post-disaster
metrics.bad: Above the limit, or raw elastic drift compared with the limit
metrics.basis: NBC 2020 4.1.8.13(2)-(3) (r1 reviewer-read); Commentary J drift discussion.
metrics.method: Multiply modal-analysis drifts (M08 model) by RdRo/IE; v1

metrics.name: Period used versus empirical cap
metrics.good: T for forces <= 2.0 x 0.05 hn^3/4 (walls), 2.0 x 0.025 hn (braced), 1.5 x empirical (moment frames); deflection periods capped at 4.0 s (walls) or 2.0 s (others)
metrics.bad: Longer period used to lower base shear; empirical Ta assumed to be conservative for stiff outrigger or transfer systems
metrics.basis: NBC 2020 4.1.8.11(3)(d): walls 244-305 m -> Ta 3.1-3.7 s, cap 6.2-7.3 s (computed). Commentary J: empirical Ta may be longer than the dynamic period.
metrics.method: Compare model T1 with caps; flag outrigger or transfer floors for dynamic analysis

metrics.name: Non-SFRS framing at 10%-in-50-year forces
metrics.good: Framing outside the SFRS elastic at 10%/50 yr forces with RdRo = 1.3 (downtown X450 Sa(0.2) 0.527, Sa(1.0) 0.198, Sa(2.0) 0.103 g)
metrics.bad: Gravity columns and slab-column connections not checked
metrics.basis: NBC 2020 4.1.8.23(4) (r1 reviewer-read, clause number to confirm); NRCan API 10%/50 yr values.
metrics.method: Route flag with explanation; hazard from the NRCan API

metrics.name: Independent review tiers
metrics.good: (a) EGBC documented independent review always; (b) special-study panel of >= 3 experts if NLDA; (c) City alternative-solution panel if unlisted SFRS or equivalence
metrics.bad: No baseline independent review, or NLDA / unlisted SFRS without the added panels
metrics.basis: EGBC bylaw quality-management standard (guide v3.0 not opened); Commentary J; Bulletin 2002-007-BU (2015). VBBL 2025 wording not read.
metrics.method: Checklist

metrics.name: PBSD acceptance (if nonlinear / alternative route)
metrics.good: Mean maximum transient story drift <= 0.03, no single record > 0.045, mean residual drift <= 0.01; service-level event 43-yr return period
metrics.bad: Exceeds these
metrics.basis: PEER TBI v2.03 values verified; adoption for Vancouver is a team assumption because NBC defines no MCER.
metrics.method: NLRHA post-processing (roadmap)

modules.method: 1) Hazard: fetch NBC 2020 values for the block lat/lon from the NRCan hazard API (CORS open) for the site designation (X_V from Vs30, class A-E, X_F); fall back to Table J-2 or pasted values; build S(T) by NBC interpolation. 2) Seismic Category from IE*S(0.2) and IE*S(1.0) (Table 4.1.8.5-B). 3) Ta empirical per 4.1.8.11(3), for seismic only; model T1 capped per (3)(d). 4) Route flags: dynamic required, wall continuity (4.1.8.10(4)), Types 4/5/6/9 from M05, non-SFRS elastic check, review tiers. 5) v1: V = S(Ta) Mv IE W/(RdRo) and Ft = 0.07 Ta V <= 0.25 V (zero if Ta <= 0.7 s); drift = elastic x RdRo/IE (x 1.2 Type 9); Vd >= 0.8 V / 1.0 V. 6) Report demand as a range across site classes. Never present as design values.
visualization: Spectrum plot: 5%-damped Sa(T) 0-10 s (log x) for selected site designations with markers at empirical Ta and model T1, a shaded 2-10 s band 'basin effects not in NBC hazard', and a grey marker for superseded NBC 2015 Sa(0.2) = 0.85 g.
Elevation with equivalent-static force arrows and Ft (v1), captioned 'screening only', and red storeys where SFRS walls break.
Route badge row (static not permitted / dynamic required / wall continuity / NLDA / review tiers), each linked to its NBC clause; SC4 SFRS table greyed by tower height.
modules.human_judgment: Site-specific hazard and ground-motion selection, SFRS choice and detailing, alternative solution or PBSD, acceptance criteria and the review panels are decisions for the engineer of record and the Chief Building Official.
modules.limits: Screening only. Defaults use X450 at downtown coordinates, not the block's measured class. NBC hazard omits Georgia-basin amplification. Soil-structure interaction, vertical motion, tall-wall shear amplification (CSA A23.3-19) and adjacency excluded. VBBL 2025 text not machine-read. VTC code compliance is advisory.

modules.name: Wind-induced motion and occupant comfort
modules.design_question: Will occupants feel the tower sway in wind, and which mix of shaping, stiffness, mass, damping or tuned mass damper brings accelerations within comfort limits?
modules.effort: ~7 person-days (NBC 4.1.7.8 wind engine, equation implementation, unit tests against the Commentary example, sensitivity UI, TMD card); after 10 Dec.
inputs: P10-M02: H, w, d, class and slenderness band
f1 and mode shape from the P10-M08 stick model (not code Ta)
Mass for wind dynamics from P10-M08 (dead load plus sustained fraction)
Vancouver q10 = 0.34 kPa and q50 = 0.45 kPa; terrain (urban = rough terrain)
Layer 0 tags of top occupied floors (residential, hotel, office)
Damping ratio preset by material; optional shape modifiers
outputs: a_across, a_along (10-yr and 1-yr), in % g and m/s2
comfort_status by occupancy and criterion
required added damping or TMD mass (t and % of building mass)
wind pressure profile p(z) = Iw q Ce Ct Cg Cp for ULS and SLS (feeds P10-M01 / M08 drift)
critical vortex-shedding speed ratio and acceleration profile for PRES

parameters.name: Natural frequency f_n
parameters.relationship: f_n up (stiffer) -> accelerations fall strongly because across-wind acceleration depends on a high power of V_H/(f_n sqrt(wd)); the ISO limit tightens as f_n rises, so softer towers are more sensitive but allowed more.

parameters.name: Damping ratio zeta
parameters.relationship: zeta up -> accelerations fall. NBC 4.1.7.8(4) values: 0.01 steel, 0.02 concrete, 0.015 composite; extra damping must come from specified devices.

parameters.name: Mass for wind dynamics (mean density rho_B)
parameters.relationship: Density up -> across-wind acceleration down (rho_B in Eq 7). Use dead load plus an editable sustained-load fraction (default 0), not seismic W; extra live mass would understate acceleration. Timber-hybrid schemes raise comfort risk.

parameters.name: Plan width w, depth d and shape
parameters.relationship: Larger w and d (lower H/sqrt(wd)) -> lower accelerations; sqrt(wd)/H < 1/3 means across-wind governs. Non-circular plans use S = 1/7, not 1/5, giving a 40% higher V_Hc; tunnel recommended (para 105).

parameters.name: Design wind (q10, q50)
parameters.relationship: Vancouver (City Hall) hourly wind pressure 0.34 kPa (1/10) and 0.45 kPa (1/50), read directly from NBC 2020 Table C-2; V = sqrt(2q/1.2929). Acceleration rises as a steep power of V_H; shielding changes results.

parameters.name: Occupancy of top floors
parameters.relationship: Residential/hotel occupants tolerate less motion than office: 1-in-10-year limits about 1.5% g (residential end) to 2.5% g (office end); motion is perceptible to most people at 0.5-1.5% g.

parameters.name: Shaping (taper, twist, setbacks, corners, openings)
parameters.relationship: Shaping can lower across-wind forces: Shanghai Tower's twist reportedly cuts wind loads 24%; Burj Khalifa's setbacks disrupt vortices; 432 Park's windbreak floors. Benefits are tunnel-dependent and not computable here.

parameters.name: Added damping (TMD mass)
parameters.relationship: TMD mass up -> effective damping up. Precedents: Taipei 101 660 t, 111 West 57th about 730 t, 432 Park two ~540 t units; mass-ratio rules not found, so sizing stays a preset.

metrics.name: Peak 1-in-10-year acceleration
metrics.good: <= 1.5% g residential/hotel; <= 2.5% g office
metrics.bad: > 3% g (above the 1-3% g preliminary range); between = conditional on occupancy
metrics.basis: NBC Commentary I para 113 (1.5-2.5% g used 1975-2000, lower for residential).
metrics.method: Eqs 7-8 with exposure and Cg per NBC 4.1.7.8

metrics.name: ISO 10137-type 1-year peak acceleration
metrics.bad: Above the curve for the occupancy
metrics.basis: Formulae for 1-year, 10-minute mean speed quoted in Commentary I para 113 (verified by reviewer); ISO 10137 itself not opened.
metrics.method: 1-year speed from V10 and V50 (Commentary Eq 9, graphic), then Eq 7-8

metrics.name: Calibration against Commentary worked example
metrics.good: Within 5% of a_W = 0.45 m/s2 (4.6% g) and a_D = 0.264 m/s2 (2.7% g) for H 183 m, w = d = 30.5 m, f 0.2 Hz, zeta 0.015, rho_B 176 kg/m3, q10 0.37 kPa (V 23.9 m/s), CeH 1.9
metrics.bad: Outside 5%
metrics.basis: Commentary I paras 63 and 115. Vancouver q10 = 0.34 kPa gives 22.9 m/s, so the example is not Vancouver data.
metrics.method: Automated unit test with rho_air = 1.2929 kg/m3

metrics.name: Wind-load engine versus Commentary I para 63 pressures
metrics.good: p = Iw q Ce Ct Cg Cp reproduces the para 63 example pressures
metrics.bad: Outside tolerance
metrics.basis: NBC 4.1.7.3(1) and 4.1.7.8(4); para 63 example values still to be transcribed from the PDF.
metrics.method: Automated unit test; ULS Iw and SLS Iw = 0.75

metrics.name: Vortex-shedding critical speed ratio V_Hc / V_H,50 (editable cut-offs)
metrics.good: >= 1.0 (resonance outside the design wind range)
metrics.bad: <= V_H at 1-year return (resonance in frequent winds)
metrics.basis: V_Hc = f_n D / S verified, S = 1/7 non-circular and 1/5 circular (Commentary I paras 104-105); cut-offs are team assumptions.
metrics.method: Compute V_Hc and compare with V_H; label 'tunnel required for non-circular'

metrics.name: Assumed damping ratio
metrics.good: 0.01 steel, 0.015 composite, 0.02 concrete
metrics.bad: Any zeta above 0.02 without a specified damper (bad side is a team assumption)
metrics.basis: NBC 4.1.7.8(4) text on amended page 4-44; Commentary I para 57.
metrics.method: Preset by material

modules.method: 1) Reference speeds from q10 = 0.34 kPa and q50 = 0.45 kPa (Table C-2; V = sqrt(2q/1.2929)); Ce(H) for rough terrain; Cg per 4.1.7.8(4) (B from w/H, s, F with x0 = 1220 fn D/VH, K = 0.10). 2) Wind engine: p = Iw q Ce Ct Cg Cp (Iw 1.0 ULS, 0.75 SLS) as a pressure profile for M01/M08 drift. 3) Across-wind a_W and along-wind a_D from Commentary I Eqs (7)-(8) for 10-yr; 1-yr via the V10/V50 relation for ISO. 4) Unit-test with the full example inputs. 5) Compare with limits by top-floor occupancy. 6) Sweep f_n, zeta, w, d, rho_B and a shape factor (tunnel-dependent). 7) If limits fail, solve added damping or TMD mass. 8) Flag the tunnel as mandatory where M02 says so. Browser-side TypeScript; output ranges, not point values.
visualization: Log-log chart of peak acceleration versus frequency with ISO-type office and residential curves, the design point, and shaded bands (below 0.5% g imperceptible, 0.5-1.5% g perceptible, above 2.5% g complaint risk).
Bar chart of a_W and a_D against limits per occupancy with pass/fail badges linked to Commentary I paragraphs.
3D tower with floors above the limit coloured red; slider panel for zeta, f_n, taper factor; TMD card showing tonnes and % of mass.
modules.human_judgment: Choice of comfort criterion (1-year versus 10-year), tolerance for occupant complaints (owner risk), reshaping versus TMD, and the wind-tunnel programme and its interpretation by the wind engineer.
modules.limits: Preliminary formulas for near-prismatic towers; tapered, twisted or interfering towers need tunnel data. Eqs (7)-(9) coefficients and Ce/Cg graphics must be verified against the PDF. Torsional motion, amplitude-dependent damping and interference are excluded; CFD cannot give specified loads.

modules.name: Core share, floor-plate efficiency, structure depth and wall continuity
modules.design_question: How much of each floor plate does the core consume, does any SFRS wall break between top and foundation, and what floor-to-floor and structure depth does the chosen system imply?
modules.effort: ~2.5 person-days for 13 Nov (storey slicing, area ratios, irregularity and continuity flags, charts).
inputs: Layer 0 floor plates and areas per storey, program tags (core, SFRS wall, circulation, mechanical, office, residential, hotel)
Tower height and storey table, including basement storeys
Optional: shaft area demand from the vertical-transport packet
Optional: structural system from P10-M01
outputs: core_ratio[storey] and net_to_gross[storey]
irregularity_flags[]: Types 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 candidates by storey
wall_continuity[storey]: red/green, plus podium advice 'make open or public space around the core, do not transfer it'
floor_to_floor and structure-depth table reconciled to H
core footprint per level for P10-M01 / M03 / M08 / M02

parameters.name: Building height and lift zoning
parameters.relationship: Taller buildings devote a larger share of floor area to structure and services (qualitative, uncited); the core steps in plan as lift banks drop out, which can trip the 130% geometric test and the continuity rule.

parameters.name: Core position / eccentricity
parameters.relationship: Core offset from the plan centre or asymmetric walls -> torsion up; NBC flags torsional sensitivity when B > 1.7, removing the simple static route and requiring 3D dynamic analysis.

parameters.name: Core continuity through podium and basement
parameters.unit: count of storeys with a wall break
parameters.relationship: An SFRS wall that ends, steps or is transferred is Type 4/5 and red under 4.1.8.10(4). Open podium or public space must wrap around the core, which also frames the human-scale ground plane.

parameters.name: Mechanical, transfer and outrigger floors
parameters.relationship: A storey heavier than 150% of an adjacent storey is a weight irregularity (Type 2). Stiff transfer or outrigger floors shorten the real period below empirical Ta (Commentary J), so Ta-based forces may be unconservative.

parameters.name: Floor-to-floor height
parameters.relationship: Floor-to-floor up (office versus residential) -> fewer storeys for the same height or a taller tower for the same GFA, raising H/w and wind load; structure depth sits inside floor-to-floor (typical values unresolved).

metrics.name: SFRS wall continuity, Type 4 (in-plane) and Type 5 (out-of-plane)
metrics.good: Every SFRS wall segment overlaps a wall segment in the storey below, down to the foundation
metrics.bad: Any segment ends, steps or shifts out of plane: red, not permitted (no NLDA route)
metrics.basis: NBC 2020 4.1.8.10(4) with Table 4.1.8.6 Types 4 and 5; Table numeric tests not re-read, so the strict continuity rule is used (r1 reviewer-read).
metrics.method: Polygon overlap of SFRS-tagged walls storey to storey; editable tolerance

metrics.name: Core ratio (core area / gross floor plate), base and typical floor (editable)
metrics.basis: No accessible primary source; starting preset for calibration against precedent plans.
metrics.method: Core polygon area / plate area per storey

metrics.name: Net-to-gross, office floors (editable)
metrics.basis: No accessible primary source; editable preset.
metrics.method: Net lettable / gross floor plate

metrics.name: Vertical geometric irregularity (Type 3)
metrics.good: SFRS horizontal dimension <= 130% of the adjacent storey
metrics.basis: NBC 2020 Table 4.1.8.6
metrics.method: Compare core/wall plan dimension between adjacent storeys

metrics.name: Weight irregularity (Type 2)
metrics.good: Storey weight <= 150% of adjacent storey (light roofs and penthouses < 10% exempt)
metrics.basis: NBC 2020 Table 4.1.8.6
metrics.method: Storey weights from M08 or area x preset

metrics.name: Vertical stiffness irregularity (Type 1, concrete walls)
metrics.good: >= 70% of adjacent storey stiffness and >= 80% of average of three storeys above/below
metrics.bad: Below either limit (other SFRS: drift > 130% of adjacent storey)
metrics.basis: NBC 2020 Table 4.1.8.6
metrics.method: Wall stiffness ratio from thickness/length per storey

metrics.name: Torsional sensitivity ratio B (Type 7)
metrics.basis: NBC 2020 Table 4.1.8.6 (B per 4.1.8.11(10), not read)
metrics.method: Needs 3D model with accidental eccentricity; plan proxy only gives a warning

modules.method: For each storey slice from Layer 0: compute A_core/A_gross and net-to-gross from program tags. Continuity: intersect each SFRS-tagged wall polygon with those of the storey below, down through the basement; any wall with no overlap is red (Types 4/5). Compare adjacent storeys for geometric (130%) and weight (150%) tests and the three storeys above/below for stiffness (concrete walls 70% / 80%). Estimate centre of mass versus centre of rigidity as a torsion warning (true B needs M08's model). Build the floor-to-floor table from editable presets per use plus structure depth, and reconcile with H. Output profiles and flags for M01, M03 and M08. Shaft areas come from the vertical-transport packet, else editable per-lift allowances.
visualization: Stacked area chart (x = storey, y = floor-plate area) split into core, circulation, net lettable and perimeter structure, with threshold lines for core ratio and net-to-gross.
Elevation strip with red ticks where wall continuity, the 130% geometric or 150% weight test fails; tooltip quotes the NBC clause or Table 4.1.8.6 type.
Plan thumbnails at base, mid and top showing core outline, SFRS walls and centre-of-mass versus centre-of-rigidity markers.
modules.human_judgment: Lift and stair strategy, how podium and public uses are organised around a continuous core, acceptable ceiling height versus structure depth, and the trade between core share and floor efficiency.
modules.limits: Core-ratio and efficiency thresholds are team assumptions. Types 4/5 use a strict continuity rule, not the Table 4.1.8.6 numeric tests. B needs a 3D model, not a plan proxy. Shaft areas need the vertical-transport module. No wall sizing or lift checks.

modules.name: Mass timber and hybrid limits checker (BCBC 2024 / VBBL 2025)
modules.design_question: Where can timber be used structurally in this tower scheme, and which BC/Vancouver limits (storeys, height, area, firewall separation, encapsulation, seismic) does it exceed?
modules.effort: ~2 person-days for 13 Nov (rule table from BCBC Table 3.2.2.93, geometry measures, zone drawing).
inputs: Layer 0: firewall-separated buildings (default: podium and tower are one building) with storeys, height to uppermost floor level, greatest horizontal area above grade
Major occupancy tags per building (A-2, B-3, C, D, E, F)
Material tags: timber floors, columns, walls; exposed timber surfaces
Seismic Category and SFRS from P10-M03 / M01
outputs: timber_zone: eligible storey range per firewall-separated building
encapsulation_tier and failing_limits[]
alternative_solution_required flag; red default for timber not firewall-separated from the tower
timber volume for P10-M08 and carbon packets

parameters.name: Storeys and height per firewall-separated building
parameters.relationship: Storeys or height up -> prescriptive EMTC ends at 18 storeys / 76 m (BCBC 3.2.2.93). Height runs from the first-storey floor to the uppermost floor level, excluding rooftop service enclosures. NBC 2020 itself stops at 12 storeys.

parameters.name: Major occupancy
parameters.relationship: Occupancy sets area cap and tiers at the 18-storey / 76 m / 70-min tier: A-2 and D 7,200 m2, C 6,000 m2 (E 12 storeys / 51 m, 6,000 m2). Groups C and D have only 70-min and 0-min tiers; no interpolation.

parameters.name: Building area (greatest horizontal area above grade)
parameters.relationship: The 79.2 x 144.8 m block (about 11,470 m2) exceeds every cap, so a timber podium must be split from the tower by firewalls, each building judged on its own area, storeys and height.

parameters.name: Firewall separation
parameters.relationship: Only a firewall creates a separate building (Div A 1.3.3.4, reviewer-read). A timber podium joined to a 300 m tower is one building and fails storeys and height at once; fire separations alone do not split it.

parameters.name: Lateral system material
parameters.relationship: Timber SFRS are capped at 20 m at SC4 (limited-ductility CLT walls, ductile-connection frames), so tall timber-framed buildings need concrete or steel cores; Brock Commons used two concrete cores for 18 storeys / 53 m.

parameters.name: Encapsulation tier and exposed timber
parameters.relationship: Lower tier (70 -> 50 -> 0 min) permits more exposed timber. At 50 min: beams/columns up to 35% of suite perimeter wall area (flame spread <= 150); ceilings 10% (<= 150) or 25% (<= 75). Top side of 70-min floors may be 50 min.

parameters.name: Fire-protection conditions
parameters.relationship: The building must be sprinklered; stair and hoistway roofs above 55 m need encapsulated-timber or concrete enclosures; above 12 storeys cladding must be noncombustible or a tested wall assembly (3.1.6.9(1)).

parameters.name: Supertall precedent
parameters.relationship: Tallest completed mass-timber building is about 86.6 m (Ascent, 25 storeys); W350 (350 m) and Oakwood (305 m) are proposals. A 244-305 m tower is outside 3.2.2.93, so structural timber there needs an alternative solution.

metrics.name: Storeys per building versus EMTC cap
metrics.good: <= 18 storeys (tier per occupancy, Table 3.2.2.93)
metrics.bad: > 18 storeys (alternative solution); the old 12-storey cap is a FALSE ASSUMPTION in BC from 2024
metrics.basis: BCBC 2024 Rev 1 Article and Table 3.2.2.93 (convenience copy read); the City RTS 16367 called it 3.2.2.91; AIBC summary.
metrics.method: Count storeys per firewall-separated building

metrics.name: Height per building (to uppermost floor level)
metrics.good: <= tier height in Table 3.2.2.93 (76 m at 18 storeys)
metrics.bad: > 76 m, or height measured to the roof instead of the uppermost floor level
metrics.basis: BCBC 3.2.2.93(1)(c): first-storey floor to uppermost floor level, excluding rooftop elevator, stair and service enclosures.
metrics.method: Measure to the uppermost floor level

metrics.name: Building area per building
metrics.good: <= 6,000 m2 (C) / 7,200 m2 (A-2, D); other occupancies per table
metrics.bad: Above the cap
metrics.basis: BCBC Table 3.2.2.93 and NBC definition of building area; VBBL 2025 numbering not machine-read.
metrics.method: Greatest horizontal area above grade

metrics.name: Firewall separation of timber from the tower
metrics.good: Timber building separated from the tower by a firewall
metrics.bad: Not firewall-separated: whole building judged at tower height, so red by default
metrics.basis: NBC 2020 Div A 1.3.3.4 note on firewalls (r1 reviewer-read).
metrics.method: Check a firewall tag on the separating plane

metrics.name: Timber SFRS height at SC4
metrics.basis: NBC 2020 Table 4.1.8.9 timber rows (SC4 column), amended page 4-63: CLT limited ductility 20 m, ductile-connection frames 20 m.
metrics.method: Table lookup

metrics.name: Exposed beams/columns share of perimeter wall (50-min tier)
metrics.basis: BCBC 3.1.6.4(3): flame-spread <= 150; walls and ceilings per (4)-(7).
metrics.method: Exposed area / perimeter wall area per suite

metrics.name: Built-precedent height ceiling (editable)
metrics.bad: > 87 m (no built precedent)
metrics.basis: Wikipedia list (secondary, 2026): Ascent 86.56 m, Mjostarnet 85.4 m, HoHo Wien 84 m; proposals above are unbuilt.
metrics.method: Compare building height

modules.method: For each firewall-separated building (default: tower and podium are one building): count storeys; measure height from the first-storey floor to the uppermost floor level excluding rooftop service enclosures; measure the greatest horizontal area above grade; read major occupancy. Look up Table 3.2.2.93 (BCBC 2024 Rev 1; VBBL numbering to confirm): storeys, height, area, encapsulation tier, no interpolation, sprinklers required. Test NBC 3.2.2.48 (12 storeys) as national baseline. Timber in a building not firewall-separated from the tower is red. Check timber SFRS against Table 4.1.8.9 SC4 heights. Compute exposed-timber shares. Draw the timber-eligible zone of podium buildings; heights above 76 m return 'alternative solution required'.
visualization: Elevation with 18-storey and 76 m cap lines; zones coloured timber-eligible / hybrid / non-combustible; firewall planes drawn.
Per-limit badges (storeys, height, area, firewall, SFRS, exposure) linked to the clause, with 'FALSE ASSUMPTION' tag on the retired 12-storey rule.
Bar showing building area versus 6,000 / 7,200 m2 caps and the 11,470 m2 site block.
modules.human_judgment: Fire-safety strategy and alternative-solution case with the Authority Having Jurisdiction; carbon and cultural intent of timber ('City in Nature', Indigenous wood protocols); whether a timber podium is worth splitting into firewall-separated buildings.
modules.limits: Table 3.2.2.93 read from the BC convenience copy (information only); VBBL 2025 numbering and amendments not machine-read. Mixed-occupancy rules, non-combustible hybrids, fire-engineering alternatives and sprinkler/cladding detail are not implemented. Heights above 76 m always need an alternative solution.

modules.name: Foundations, below-grade levels and transit link
modules.design_question: What foundation concept and basement depth fit this load in downtown Vancouver, how must the below-grade transit link be separated or connected seismically, and what must the geotechnical engineer and transit owner confirm?
modules.effort: ~3 person-days for 10 Dec (link joint check, foundation clause flags, site designation, section drawing); raft pressures and quantities follow on the roadmap.
inputs: Footprints of tower raft and podium; number of below-grade levels (parking, loading, transit link) from Layer 0 tags
Tower drift at link level from P10-M03 (x RdRo/IE) and user-entered station drift
Optional: weight W (M08) and overturning moments from wind (M04) and seismic (M03)
User-entered geotechnical data: Vs30, layers, groundwater level, allowable bearing
Neighbouring station envelope and link level (user-drawn polygon)

excavation_depth, excavation_volume, shoring_perimeter
q_mean, e/B, contact-area ratio (when M08 exists)
site_designation (X_V, X_S, X_F) for P10-M03

parameters.name: Soil stiffness (Vs30) and deposit type
parameters.relationship: Metro Vancouver mean Vs30 is 334 m/s; upland glacial till 360-580 m/s versus post-glacial/delta sediments 180-250 m/s. Lower Vs30 -> higher site class and seismic demand; bearing and settlement need geotechnical confirmation.

parameters.name: Overturning moment and foundation rules
parameters.relationship: e = M/W up as H up or base width down. NBC 4.1.8.16(2): ALL foundations must exceed SFRS lateral capacity; (3) caps demand at RdRo = 1.0 forces with 1.5x bearing and 1.3x other resistances; (4) relaxes only for foundations not constrained against rotation; (6) SC4 ties and piles.

parameters.name: Number of basement levels
parameters.relationship: Levels up -> excavation depth, shoring and dewatering up; walls and diaphragms through below-grade levels make the structure 'constrained', which changes how base shear and overturning are carried.

parameters.name: Liquefiable or soft soils
parameters.relationship: Liquefiable soil, sensitive clay, thick peat or more than 30 m of soft clay -> site designation X_F (site-specific response or ground improvement); measured Vs30 gives X_V and avoids the extra conservatism of X_S.

parameters.name: Adjacent transit station and link
parameters.relationship: NBC 4.1.8.14: adjacent structures need a gap of at least the SRSS of their deflections (tower drift x RdRo/IE, station drift), or a connected design with the lowest RdRo and a special study if non-rigid. Transit protection zones and vibration also apply.

parameters.name: Basin and long-period effects
parameters.relationship: NBC 2020 hazard does not model Georgia-basin amplification, which UBC simulations suggest raises long-period demand on tall concrete shear-wall buildings; soft sediments deeper than 30 m may need site-specific analysis.

parameters.name: Podium and basement diaphragms (backstay)
parameters.relationship: Stiff basement walls and podium diaphragms carry core shear to the perimeter below grade (backstay), raising diaphragm and wall demand and changing foundation moments; the effect is not computed here.

metrics.name: Seismic joint at the transit link
metrics.good: Gap >= SRSS(tower drift x RdRo/IE, station drift) at link level, or a connected design using the lowest RdRo
metrics.bad: Gap below SRSS, or a rigid connection without special study
metrics.basis: NBC 2020 4.1.8.14 (r1 reviewer-read, 2nd printing); station drift is user input.
metrics.method: SRSS of the two deflections at link level

metrics.name: Foundation resistance versus SFRS overturning capacity
metrics.good: All foundations exceed SFRS lateral capacity (4.1.8.16(2)); demand capped per (3) with 1.5x bearing and 1.3x other resistances
metrics.bad: Resistance below capacity, or the (4) relaxation used for a foundation constrained against rotation
metrics.basis: NBC 2020 4.1.8.16(2)-(4) and (6) (r1 reviewer-read); Commentary J on constrained structures.
metrics.method: Compare capacity-protected SFRS base moment with foundation resistance

metrics.name: Basis of site designation
metrics.good: X_V from in-situ Vs30 measurements
metrics.bad: X_S from SPT / undrained strength (adds conservatism)
metrics.basis: NBC 4.1.8.4(2)-(3); Commentary J Fig J-10 text.
metrics.method: Check input type

metrics.name: Base eccentricity e/B under service wind (editable)
metrics.good: <= 1/6 (inside the kern, no uplift)
metrics.basis: Statics; no code source applied; seismic and ULS cases may accept partial uplift with analysis.
metrics.method: e = M/W on rigid raft

metrics.name: Mean bearing pressure versus geotechnical allowable
metrics.good: <= value supplied by the geotechnical engineer
metrics.bad: > that value
metrics.basis: No default allowable; downtown till properties unverified.
metrics.method: q = W / A_f

metrics.name: Basement depth / levels
metrics.good: No sourced limit; set by geotechnical, groundwater and transit-interface constraints
metrics.bad: No sourced limit
metrics.basis: No Vancouver threshold found. Anchor: Living Shangri-La excavation 26 m, deepest in Vancouver at the time (secondary).
metrics.method: n x storey height + raft depth

metrics.name: Transit-owner approval and vibration isolation
metrics.good: TransLink/BCRTC approval checklist started and vibration isolation addressed
metrics.bad: Link drawn only as a clearance polygon
metrics.basis: No transit guideline found; City of Vancouver and EGBC pages returned 403 and searches were exhausted.
metrics.method: Checklist

modules.method: 1) Link check: take tower drift at link level from M03 (elastic x RdRo/IE), user-entered station drift; required joint = SRSS of the two; or set 'connected' and use the lower RdRo. 2) Foundation flags per 4.1.8.16(2)-(4), (6). 3) Derive site designation from Vs30 (X_V) or SPT/strength class (X_S) and flag X_F triggers. 4) Excavation depth = n x basement storey height + raft thickness (editable); volume = A_f x depth. 5) Intersect the basement polygon with the station envelope and report clearance. 6) When M08/M04 exist: q_mean = W/A_f, e = M/W, contact-area ratio on a rigid raft. 7) Emit investigation, vibration and TransLink/BCRTC checklists. Concept labels (raft, piled raft, caissons) are team-assumption mappings shown as questions.
visualization: Section through tower and basement with soil layers coloured by Vs30 band, groundwater line, excavation outline and the link joint drawn with its required width.
Plan with false-colour contact-pressure contours under the raft (kPa legend) and kern outline (roadmap).
Conflict overlay: basement polygon versus station envelope with red hatch where clearance is below the user minimum or the joint is under SRSS.
modules.human_judgment: Geotechnical engineer's call on bearing, settlement, piles or caissons, dewatering and shoring; transit owner approval and vibration criteria for works beside the station; construction sequencing (top-down versus bottom-up).
modules.limits: No soil, groundwater or station data built in; downtown bedrock depth and till properties unverified. No settlement, soil-structure interaction, dewatering or ground-movement analysis. Concept mapping is an editable assumption. Results frame questions for the geotechnical engineer and transit owner.

parameters.name: System choice and height
parameters.relationship: Taller or more slender -> more structural material per m2 because stiffness governs; historical steel use runs from about 145 kg/m2 (John Hancock trussed tube) to 206 (Empire State) and 275 kg/m2 (One Chase Manhattan Plaza).

parameters.name: Gravity live loads
parameters.relationship: Minimum office live load 2.4 kPa, 4.8 kPa for basement and ground-level office floors (Table 4.1.5.3; Note A-4.1.5.11). Live load up -> slab and column quantities up, but NOT seismic weight W.

parameters.name: Seismic weight W
parameters.relationship: W = dead load (partition allowance not above 0.5 kPa) + 25% snow + 60% storage load + tank contents (4.1.8.2). Heavier W raises base shear and overturning; ordinary live load is excluded.

parameters.name: Mass for wind dynamics
parameters.relationship: Dead load plus an editable sustained-load fraction (default 0). More mass lowers predicted wind accelerations, so adding ordinary live load would be unconservative; M04 reads this preset, not W.

parameters.name: Wind drift limit
parameters.relationship: Limit hs/500 per storey under service wind (Iw = 0.75): required lateral stiffness scales inversely with the limit, so a tighter limit means thicker walls or more outrigger steel. H/500 is only a secondary guide.

parameters.name: Seismic demand V/W
parameters.relationship: V/W from M03 (inverse of Rd x Ro) sets wall shear and reinforcement demand; SC4 requires ductile detailing, which raises reinforcement density (value unresolved).

parameters.name: Perimeter or diagrid systems
parameters.relationship: Reported savings: Hearst Tower diagrid about 21% less steel than a standard frame; Shanghai Tower about 25% less structural steel than a conventional design. Project claims, not generic factors.

parameters.name: Timber share
parameters.relationship: Timber share up -> concrete and seismic weight down, but wind acceleration risk up as density falls (rho_B in Eq 7); the lateral system stays concrete or steel at SC4.

metrics.name: Seismic weight W definition
metrics.good: W = dead load (partitions not above 0.5 kPa) + 25% snow + 60% storage + tank contents
metrics.bad: Adds ordinary office or residential live load
metrics.basis: NBC 2020 4.1.8.2 (r1 reviewer-read); live loads from Table 4.1.5.3, not Commentary A.
metrics.method: Per-storey sum of presets

metrics.name: Service-wind drift utilisation (required EI / provided EI at hs/500)
metrics.good: <= 1.0 at every storey
metrics.bad: > 1.0 at any storey
metrics.basis: NBC 2020 4.1.3.5(3) (r1 reviewer quote); pressures per 4.1.7.8; H/500 only a Commentary I guide.
metrics.method: Equivalent cantilever or stick model under p = Iw q Ce Ct Cg Cp from the M04 engine (Iw 0.75)

metrics.name: Steel-equivalent kg/m2 versus historical band (editable)
metrics.good: Within or below 145-275 kg/m2 for steel-framed towers
metrics.bad: > 275 kg/m2 (heavier than the 1961 One Chase Manhattan Plaza)
metrics.basis: 1930s-1960s anchors (secondary), used as editable thresholds because no modern benchmark was accessible.
metrics.method: Total steel-equivalent / GFA

metrics.name: Concrete and rebar intensity anchor (editable)
metrics.good: Within +/-30% of 0.83 m3 concrete/m2 and 114 kg rebar/m2 (Living Shangri-La, about 197 m)
metrics.bad: Outside +/-50% or uncalibrated
metrics.basis: Wikipedia (secondary): 51,000 m3 concrete, 7,000 t rebar, 61,300 m2 floor area; one tower only.
metrics.method: Quantities / GFA, then calibrate to at least 3 precedents

metrics.name: Uncertainty band of totals (editable)
metrics.good: <= +/-30% after calibration to at least 3 precedent towers
metrics.bad: > +/-50% or uncalibrated
metrics.basis: No source; planning preset.
metrics.method: Monte Carlo over presets

modules.method: 1) Build a storey table from Layer 0 (GFA by use, plate area, core area from M05). 2) Gravity: NBC live loads plus preset dead loads (editable) -> slab thickness from a span table, columns from tributary load and a stress limit. 3) Seismic weight W per 4.1.8.2; wind mass = dead load + sustained fraction. 4) Lateral: required effective EI so every storey's service-wind drift <= hs/500 (M04 engine, cracked-section EI per 4.1.8.3(8)(a)); check M03 V/W against preset wall shear capacity. 5) Add outrigger/belt steel, foundations (M07), basement walls; warn on differential shortening. 6) Convert to m3 concrete, t rebar, t steel, m3 timber (M06). 7) Monte Carlo for P10/P50/P90; export densities and weights for M03/M04. 8) Calibrate to precedent tallies.
visualization: Stacked bar of material by element class (slabs, columns, core, outriggers, foundations) and storey band, with P10-P90 whiskers.
Sankey from massing to quantities to embodied-carbon handoff.
Tornado chart of sensitivity to presets and scatter of kg/m2 versus H with historical anchors; every value tagged verified / team assumption.
modules.human_judgment: Engineer's sizing and detailing, concrete versus steel versus hybrid trade-offs, cost and carbon decisions, and the tolerance the team accepts for early estimates.
modules.limits: Order-of-magnitude only; presets are unsourced team assumptions; no post-tensioning, transfers, connections, creep or construction sequence; outrigger effectiveness approximated. Steel kg/m2 anchors are 1960s, not modern benchmarks. Calibrate with real tallies before quoting cost or carbon.

flags.claim: Vancouver seismic design uses NBC 2015 / VBBL 2019 values (Sa(0.2) about 0.85 g, Class C).
flags.correction: NBC 2020 X450 Sa(0.2) = 1.1 g (+25%) and Sa(2.0) = 0.27 g (+5%); VBBL 2025 seismic rules apply to new Vancouver projects from 15 Sep 2026 (in force on 21 Oct 2026); in-stream projects may use old rules until 8 Mar 2027.
flags.detail: Sources P10-S01, P10-S03, P10-S05, P10-S09. VTC is hypothetical, so use NBC 2020 values as advisory. r1: NRCan API gives downtown X450 Sa(0.2) = 1.04 g (P10-S43); BC bulletin P10-S42 confirms the 8 Mar 2027 in-stream date.

flags.claim: Encapsulated mass timber in BC is limited to 12 storeys.
flags.correction: BCBC 2024 Revision 1 and VBBL 2025 allow 18 storeys / 76 m with 70-minute encapsulation and area caps of 6,000 m2 (C) and 7,200 m2 (D, A-2); NBC 2020 itself remains at 12 storeys.
flags.detail: Sources P10-S04, P10-S06, P10-S07. r1: table now read directly in BCBC Table 3.2.2.93 (P10-S40); Groups C and D have only 70-min and 0-min tiers.

flags.claim: CFD can replace wind-tunnel testing for specified wind loads or comfort.
flags.correction: NBC 2020 Div B 4.1.7.1(6) states CFD shall not be used to determine specified wind loads; the Wind Tunnel Procedure is mandatory for very dynamically sensitive buildings (f1 <= 0.25 Hz, or occupied H/w > 6) and where wake buffeting is possible.
flags.detail: Source P10-S04. r1: 4.1.7.1(4) and (6) re-read on amended page 4-29 (P10-S45).

flags.claim: Outrigger, belt-truss, diagrid or mega-frame systems are code-listed SFRS with Rd and Ro values.
flags.correction: No such SFRS appears in NBC 2020 Vol. 1 (text search); unlisted systems use Rd = Ro = 1.0 unless equivalence is proven by cyclic tests, NLDA, equivalent collapse margin and independent peer review; 'other' SFRS are not permitted at SC3-SC4.
flags.detail: Sources P10-S04, P10-S05 (paras 213-214). Search covered machine-read text only. See also the r1 refinement that outrigger schemes are not automatically 'unlisted'.

flags.claim: The equivalent static method is adequate for a 244-305 m tower.
flags.correction: It is permitted only for SC1-SC2, regular buildings under 60 m with Ta < 2 s, or irregular buildings under 20 m with Ta < 0.5 s; Vancouver is SC4, so dynamic analysis is required.

flags.claim: Moderately ductile concrete walls or steel braced frames can serve a tall Vancouver tower.
flags.correction: At SC4 moderately ductile concrete shear/coupled walls are capped at 60 m and moderately ductile steel CBF or BRB at 40 m; only ductile walls, coupled walls, MRF, EBF and plate walls have no height limit.
flags.detail: Source P10-S04 Table 4.1.8.9 (machine-read; confirm in PDF). r1 refinement (reviewer): ductile BRBF (Rd 4.0) is capped at 40 m at SC4; concrete moderately ductile MRF 40 m; moderately ductile plate walls 40 m; steel moderately ductile MRF no limit. Load the whole SC4 column into JSON.

flags.claim: NBC 2020 ground motions already include Georgia-basin amplification.
flags.correction: Commentary J states the NBC 2020 hazard model does not take basin effects into account and has no basin maps; UBC simulations indicate underestimation for tall shear-wall buildings.
flags.detail: Sources P10-S05, P10-S11. Consider site-specific analysis for towers.

flags.claim: Core walls may be transferred or terminated at the podium if nonlinear dynamic analysis is done (P10-M01).
flags.correction: NBC 4.1.8.10(4): where Ta >= 1.0 s and IE*S(1.0) > 0.25, non-wood SFRS shear walls run continuously from top to foundation with no Type 4 or 5 irregularity. Downtown X450 S(1.0) = 0.43 g and every 244-305 m tower has Ta > 1 s. Open podium spaces go around the core.
flags.detail: Raised in r1 as BLOCKER. Clause text read by the independent reviewer in the 2nd printing; not re-opened here (P10-S04). Not corrected by the 2025 errata (P10-S45).

flags.claim: NBC wind serviceability limit is top drift <= H/500 under q50 = 0.45 kPa (P10-M01, P10-M08).
flags.correction: Check total drift per storey <= hs/500 under service wind (Iw SLS = 0.75) with Dynamic Procedure pressures p = Iw q Ce Ct Cg Cp. Keep H/250-H/1000 only as Commentary I guidance.
flags.detail: NBC 2020 4.1.3.5(3): the total drift per storey under service wind and gravity loads shall not exceed 1/500 of the storey height (reviewer quote); Table 4.1.7.3 gives Iw SLS = 0.75. Bare q50 omits Ce, Cg and Cp, understating load several times.

flags.claim: Stiff transfer floors acting as outriggers lengthen the real period versus the empirical formulas (P10-M01, P10-M05).
flags.correction: Transfers or outrigger floors can shorten the real period below empirical Ta, so forces based on Ta may be unconservative. Flag the case for dynamic analysis.
flags.detail: Commentary J (p. J-70): the empirical period may be longer than the dynamic-analysis period for stiff transfer floors acting as outriggers (reviewer quote). Source P10-S05.

flags.claim: Strouhal number is about 1/5 for buildings (P10-M02, P10-M04).
flags.correction: Use S = 1/7 for rectangular or polygonal plans and 1/5 only for circular plans; label non-circular results 'tunnel required' (para 105).
flags.detail: Commentary I paras 104-105 (P10-S05). Arithmetic note: V_Hc = f_n D / S is 40% higher with S = 1/7, so using 1/5 understated V_Hc by about 29%; the reviewer wrote 'overstates'. S = 1/7 applied either way.

flags.claim: Higher live load raises seismic weight W (P10-M08).
flags.correction: W = dead load (partitions need not exceed 0.5 kPa) + 25% snow + 60% storage load + tank contents. Ordinary live load is excluded; wind-dynamics mass is a separate preset.
flags.detail: NBC 2020 Div B 4.1.8.2 (reviewer-read). Including live load inflates V and rho_B; a higher rho_B lowers predicted wind accelerations, which is unconservative.

flags.claim: The Commentary I worked example speeds (23.9 m/s) confirm the Vancouver Table C-2 column mapping (q10 = 0.34 kPa).
flags.correction: q10 = 0.34 and q50 = 0.45 kPa are correct, but because they appear directly in the NBC 2020 Table C-2 Vancouver (City Hall) row, not because they match the example.
flags.detail: The example uses q10 = 0.37 kPa and rho_B = 176 kg/m3: 23.9 = sqrt(2 x 370 / 1.2929). Vancouver 0.34 kPa gives 22.9 m/s (P10-S04, P10-S05).

flags.claim: Mass-timber EMTC height is measured from the first-storey floor to the roof, and 'fire-separated parts' can be checked as separate buildings (P10-M06).
flags.correction: Height runs to the uppermost floor level, excluding rooftop service enclosures. Only firewalls create separate buildings, so a timber podium joined to the tower is the same building.
flags.detail: BCBC 3.2.2.93(1)(c) read directly (P10-S40); firewall rule from NBC 2020 Div A 1.3.3.4 (reviewer-read, P10-S04).

flags.claim: Type 9 irregularity requires nonlinear dynamic analysis (P10-M01, P10-M03).
flags.correction: NLDA with vertical motion is required only when alpha exceeds twice the Type 9 limit and IE*S(0.2) >= 0.5. Otherwise drift is multiplied by 1.2. Limits: alpha 0.1 (self-centering), 0.03 (other).
flags.detail: NBC 2020 Table 4.1.8.6 Type 9; 4.1.8.10(7)-(9) (reviewer-read, P10-S04).

flags.claim: Independent structural review is needed only when NLDA or an unlisted SFRS is used (P10-M03).
flags.correction: Baseline documented independent review is always required in BC (EGBC bylaw quality-management standard); the Commentary J special-study panel (NLDA) and the City alternative-solution panel (unlisted) come on top.
flags.detail: Reviewer search summary of EGBC statements; guide v3.0 (June 2023) not opened and egbc.ca returned 403 here (P10-S47).

flags.claim: Modal-analysis seismic drifts can be compared directly with 0.025 hs (P10-M03).
flags.correction: Elastic deflections including accidental torsion are multiplied by RdRo/IE (and by 1.2 for Type 9) before comparison with the limit; add Vd >= 0.8 V (regular) / 1.0 V (irregular).
flags.detail: NBC 2020 4.1.8.13(2)-(3), 4.1.8.10(8), 4.1.8.12(8)-(9) (reviewer-read). For ductile walls RdRo = 5.6, so raw drift is understated more than fivefold.

flags.claim: Code empirical Ta can supply f1 for wind classification, and H/w <= 4 coloured green means no tunnel is needed (P10-M02).
flags.correction: Ta is for seismic loads only. Use a dynamic-model f1; default tunnel_required = true for H >= about 180 m without one. Colour by the governing trigger.
flags.detail: Commentary J: empirical Ta is only for estimating seismic design loads, not wind. Wall Ta of 3.1-3.7 s (0.27-0.32 Hz) would wrongly avoid the tunnel. H > 60 m is dynamically sensitive regardless of H/w (P10-S45).

flags.claim: Any outrigger scheme is an unlisted SFRS with Rd = Ro = 1.0 (P10-M01).
flags.correction: Core walls are the listed SFRS; outriggers and belts are capacity-protected elements; combined systems take the lowest RdRo (4.1.8.9(3)) or show equivalence (4.1.8.9(5)). Use three route states: listed + outrigger elements, equivalence, unlisted.
flags.detail: Reviewer reading of NBC 4.1.8.9; special study is still likely (P10-S04, P10-S05).

flags.claim: Structural system-height envelopes (core-outrigger, belt truss, mega-frame, diagrid, buttressed core) used in P10-M01.
flags.detail: CVU/CTBUH guides are paywalled and Ali and Moon (2007) was not opened; only secondary statements (tubes above 40 storeys, shear-wall frame to 70 storeys) were found. Presets are editable team assumptions.

flags.claim: When Vancouver requires performance-based seismic design or structural peer review for tall buildings under VBBL 2025.
flags.detail: VBBL 2025 Book I PDFs are scanned images and could not be machine-read; only Bulletin 2002-007-BU (2015) and the 2025 guide were read. Ask the Chief Building Official's office or read Division B 4.1 and Division C 2.3 manually.

flags.claim: Which hazard level represents MCER for performance-based design in Canada.
flags.detail: TBI v2.03 uses ASCE 7 MCER; NBC uses the 2%-in-50-year uniform hazard spectrum with Rd and Ro. The TBI drift limits are therefore a team-assumption preset until an EGBC or VBBL criterion is found.

flags.claim: OpenSees / OpenSeesPy licence versus an open-source hosted web tool.
flags.detail: OpenSees permits educational, research and non-profit use and otherwise internal use only; OpenSeesPy bars commercial redistribution and cloud services without a licence (P10-S22, P10-S23). Use only offline for validation or obtain permission.

flags.claim: Downtown Vancouver site class, till properties, bedrock depth and groundwater at the VTC block.
flags.detail: Only municipal averages were found (mean Vs30 334 m/s; till near surface; rock shallower in northern Vancouver). A geotechnical report is required; the microzonation hub (P10-S14) is JavaScript-only and must be checked manually for the block.

flags.claim: TransLink / BCRTC protection zones, vibration limits and tunnel-interface rules for development beside the transit station and the below-grade link (P10-M07).
flags.detail: No guideline found; searches were exhausted and City of Vancouver and EGBC pages returned 403. NBC 4.1.8.14 gives the seismic joint rule only. Ask the transit owner.

flags.claim: Quantity presets, TMD sizing, foundation-concept mapping, eccentricity limits, basement thresholds and the sustained-load fraction in P10-M04, M07 and M08.
flags.detail: All are editable presets with no accessible source; historical steel kg/m2 anchors (145 / 206 / 275) come from secondary 1930s-1960s buildings. The Living Shangri-La anchor (0.83 m3/m2, 114 kg/m2) is one secondary data point.
